header: DOES A NEW OR CHANGED LINE CLASH WITH A SAVED ONE? (step 64a; my rule, 31 Oct 2026: "no entry must conflict with any currently saved one: inform him and ask whether he wants to edit an existing one or has made a mistake"). PURE. Three kinds of clash, each with its own way out: same-number the number is already assigned to another line. No way through: the number belongs to one place. Edit the saved line, or correct the entry. same-place the department and the location are already saved (with another number). Maybe a SECOND number of the same place ("40926 / 42043"): he may say so. Or edit the saved line, or correct the entry. similar-place a saved place that reads almost the same (a spelling slip, "Gate No. 2" for "Gate No. 2A", the words in another order). Maybe a different place: he may say so. Or edit, or correct. The saved lines are named in the table's own words (department, location): I use the same splitting the search table uses (display.ts).

symbols.name: locationKey
doc: "Office" and "no location" are the same place: the table shows Office for an empty location.

symbols.name: wordsOf
symbols.sig: const wordsOf = (department: string, location: string): string[] =>
doc: These are the words actually written. An empty location adds none, because the word Office of the table is only a stand-in and would stop "CISF Tumla Gate" reading like "CISF" / "Tumla Gate".

symbols.name: readAlike
symbols.sig: function readAlike(a: string[], b: string[]): boolean
doc: Both ways every word has a counterpart (the same word, a short number and the same number with a letter, a slip of one letter): then I say the two places read alike.

symbols.name: savedLines
doc: The saved lines in the table's own words. I leave out lines without an id (never read from the table), since nothing can be edited without one.

members.name: ignoreId
doc: The line being changed; it never clashes with itself.

members.name: keepsNumber
doc: When a line is changed and keeps its number, I do not check the number again (42043 stands on two lines already, and changing the location of one must stay possible).

symbols.name: describeLine
doc: This gives the words the panel shows for a saved line: "CISF · Tumla Gate · 40926".

symbols.name: acknowledgementCovers
symbols.sig: export function acknowledgementCovers(conflicts: PaxConflict[], acks: Acknowledge[] = []): boolean
doc: May the person go on after answering? My rule: a number is never shared. The other two clashes may be answered, each by its own answer and only when it is true: "second-number" = another number of the same place; "different" = a different place that merely reads alike.
